## 3. The main event: Phase 2 — Core OPD Flow

**Goal, verbatim from `phases.md`:** a single clinic can fully run OPD: register a patient, doctor sees them, writes a note, prescribes, billing captures the charge. **This phase alone should be a shippable Tier 1 product.**

This is a bigger phase than Phase 1 — 7ish new tables instead of 2, 2 Edge Functions, and a genuine domain-correctness question in billing (§3.6 below). Apply the same rigor as Phase 1: every table ships with RLS in the migration that creates it, every RLS claim gets a real test against real Postgres, migrations are additive history, no service-role key outside a local dev script. Reuse and extend the PGlite harness and remote-suite pattern already built (`supabase/tests/harness/`, `supabase/tests/local/`, `supabase/tests/remote/`) rather than inventing a second testing approach.

### 3.1 `patients`

Suggested starting shape — adjust if you find a real reason, document what changed and why in the contract file (§3.8):

- `id uuid pk`, `tenant_id uuid not null references tenants(id)`
- `full_name text not null`, `phone text`, `dob date`, `gender text`, `address text`
- `allergies text` (free text is fine for this phase; a structured allergy table only if your interaction-check design in §3.4 needs it relationally)
- `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`

**Duplicate handling:** `Workflow.md`'s own worked example for this exact feature specifies "duplicate phone number within tenant → `DUPLICATE_PATIENT`." Treat `(tenant_id, phone)` as the uniqueness scope, but decide what happens when `phone` is null (a walk-in with no phone, or a child registered under a guardian's number who isn't a duplicate in any meaningful sense) — a naive unique index will misbehave here. Document your choice.

RLS: standard tenant-scoped read/write for staff roles (`admin`, `doctor`, `nurse`, `billing`); `patient` role should not have blanket read access to the `patients` table itself in this phase (a patient-portal "my own record" view is not in this phase's scope — don't build it, don't block on it).

### 3.2 `visits`

- `id uuid pk`, `tenant_id`, `patient_id references patients(id)`, `doctor_id references profiles(id)` (nullable until assigned)
- `visit_type text` (`new` / `follow_up`), `status text` (`queued` / `in_consultation` / `done`, at minimum)
- `created_at`, and whatever timestamps make sense for a queue/wait-time view (PRD §6.1 wants a wait-time indicator)

This table is also where `phases.md` Phase 3 will later add IPD admit/discharge status. **Don't build that now** — but don't pick column names or a status enum so narrow that extending it later means a rename instead of an addition. A short comment noting "IPD extension point, Phase 3" is enough; no need to design IPD's columns today.

### 3.3 `clinical_notes`

**The one hard constraint that matters more than anything else in this table:** `rules.md` §1.7 — *"No mandatory form fields on doctor-facing clinical notes that would block saving... enforce at the schema level with nullable columns, not `NOT NULL` constraints, for clinical free-text fields."* This is a product requirement, not a style preference. Every clinical free-text column here must be nullable. A doctor must be able to save an empty or half-filled note. Say explicitly in your report which columns you made nullable and confirm none of them block a save.

- `id`, `tenant_id`, `visit_id references visits(id)`, `doctor_id`
- `note_text text` (nullable), maybe a `template_type text` if you want structure — nullable too
- `created_at`

### 3.4 `prescriptions` + `prescription_items` + a minimal drug reference

- `prescriptions`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `visit_id`, `doctor_id`, `created_at`
- `prescription_items`: `id`, `prescription_id`, `drug_name`, `is_generic boolean`, `dose text`, `frequency text`, `duration text`
- A small **starter** drug reference table (name, generic name, common interaction/allergy tags) — seed a basic Indian drug list, on the order of dozens of common OPD drugs, not hundreds. **Explicitly label this in a comment and in the contract as a starter dataset for interaction-checking, not a certified/exhaustive drug database** — nobody downstream should mistake this for something it isn't.

**Interaction/allergy check — the part that needs to match PRD language exactly.** PRD §6.1 and `rules.md` §6.4: *"Silent-by-default interaction/allergy checking; hard interrupt only for high-severity combinations."* And `rules.md` §3.4: a failed safety check must fail loud ("verify manually"), never silently look like a passed one.

Concretely, this means:
- Design a function (e.g. `check_prescription_safety(p_patient_id uuid, p_drug_names text[])`) that returns **a severity per finding**, not a boolean. Something like a set of `{ finding_type: 'interaction' | 'allergy', severity: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high', description, drug_a, drug_b }` rows. The severity field is the contract — Prince's UI decides modal-vs-inline-badge based on it, per `Design.md` §9's own checklist item. If you only return true/false, you've made the UI decision for him and taken away the thing the product requirement actually needs.
- If the check itself errors (bad input, missing drug in reference table, whatever), that must be distinguishable from "checked, found nothing" — don't let an error path quietly return an empty result set that looks identical to a clean bill of health.

### 3.5 `billing_line_items` + auto-insert trigger

- `billing_line_items`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `patient_id`, `visit_id`, `source_type text` (e.g. `consultation`, `medicine`, `lab` — even though lab is Phase 3, leave room), `description`, `amount numeric`, `tax_category` and `tax_rate` **per line item** — see §3.6, this is not optional, `created_at`
- A trigger (or triggers) that auto-inserts a line item when a chargeable event happens — at minimum, a visit/consultation being marked and a prescription being saved. `phases.md`'s Definition of Done is specific here: *"Billing charges auto-appear with zero manual entry by billing staff."* If billing staff would need to manually add a line item for a normal consultation, this isn't done yet.

### 3.6 `invoices` — read this before designing the GST handling

I looked this up rather than assuming, because getting it wrong here would ship an incorrect invoice, not just an incomplete one.

Under GST Notification No. 12/2017 (Central Tax – Rate), core healthcare services — diagnosis, treatment, and care provided by a clinical establishment or an authorised medical practitioner — are **GST-exempt**. Medicines and pharmacy dispensing are a **separate, taxable** category: following the GST Council's September 2025 reform, most drugs sit at a uniform 5% slab, with a specific list of life-saving drugs fully exempted ([ClearTax: GST on Medicines and Pharmaceuticals](https://cleartax.in/s/impact-of-gst-rate-on-pharmaceutical-industry); [Taxmann: GST on Healthcare Services](https://www.taxmann.com/post/blog/gst-on-healthcare-services)). Content paraphrased from these sources for compliance with reproduction limits.

**Practical consequence for your schema:** a single OPD invoice that bundles a consultation fee with dispensed medicines is mixing an exempt line and a taxable line on the same document. Applying one flat GST rate to the invoice total would be wrong, not just imprecise — this is exactly why `billing_line_items` needs `tax_category`/`tax_rate` at the **line-item** level (§3.5), and `invoices` needs to sum tax per category, not apply a single rate to a grand total.

One more thing you can't resolve alone: whether a given tenant charges GST **at all** depends on whether that clinic is GST-registered, which in turn depends on annual turnover (₹20 lakh threshold generally, ₹10 lakh in a few special-category states — [Tax2Win: GST for Doctors in India](https://tax2win.in/guide/gst-for-doctors-india)). A solo doctor under the threshold may legitimately issue a non-GST bill. **Don't hardcode "GST always applies."** Add a per-tenant setting (a boolean or registration-status field on `tenants`, or a sensible default you document) that governs whether tax lines are computed at all, and flag this explicitly to Jeet as a business decision he needs to confirm per real pilot clinic — not something you can determine from code alone.

- `invoices`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `patient_id`, `visit_id`, references/aggregates the line items, `subtotal`, `tax_total`, `grand_total`, `created_at`. Exact shape is yours to design well; the constraint above (per-category tax, not flat-rate) is the part that isn't negotiable.

### 3.7 Edge Functions

- `generate-prescription-pdf` — per `rules.md` §3.7, wrap in try/catch, return `{ error: { code, message } }` structured responses, never a raw stack trace.
- `generate-invoice-pdf` — GST-compliant per §3.6's per-line tax treatment. If a tenant has GST disabled (per the setting above), the generated invoice should render as a legitimate non-GST bill, not a GST invoice with zeros awkwardly present.

### 3.8 RLS, tests, and contracts — same bar as Phase 1

- Every table above: RLS enabled in the migration that creates it, tested against real Postgres (extend `supabase/tests/local/`), and re-verified against the hosted project (extend `supabase/tests/remote/`) the same way Phase 1's suites work. Include a negative control at least once for this phase's new tables, the same way the Phase 1 suite proved its own passes weren't vacuous — you don't need one per table if a shared negative-control pattern covers the group.
- Write **4 contract files** in `docs/contracts/` per `Workflow.md`'s format, so Prince can build against them with `NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_MOCK=true` without waiting on you: `patient-registration.md`, `opd-queue.md`, `prescriptions.md`, `billing.md`. Follow `auth-tenancy.md`'s structure (table shapes, RPC/function signatures, the two-error-channel explanation if you keep the `{ok, code, message}` envelope pattern, error-code table, TypeScript types for the mock layer). Decide per-function whether the envelope pattern from Phase 1 is still the right call here or whether plain table operations suffice for straightforward CRUD (registration, note-taking) and reserve the envelope for things with real business-rule branching (safety checks, billing calc) — your call, document it.
- Error codes to cover at minimum: duplicate patient (§3.1), prescription save failure, safety-check-unavailable (per `rules.md` §3.4 — this needs its own distinguishable code, not a generic failure).

### Definition of Done (from `phases.md`, this is what "done" means)

- [ ] Full OPD loop works end-to-end for one tenant: register → queue → consult → prescribe → bill
- [ ] Prescription and invoice PDFs generate correctly
- [ ] Billing charges auto-appear with zero manual entry by billing staff
- [ ] Cross-tenant isolation re-verified with every new table (local + remote)
- [ ] Interaction/allergy check returns severity, not a boolean; silent-by-default is possible for the UI to implement from what you return
- [ ] No `NOT NULL` on any clinical free-text column
- [ ] Per-line-item tax treatment in billing; per-tenant GST-applicability setting exists and is documented as a business decision for Jeet, not a hardcoded assumption
- [ ] 4 contract files written
- [ ] `Memory.md` updated (§1 correction from this prompt, plus this phase's decisions/state/risks)
- [ ] `supabase/types/database.types.ts` regenerated against the hosted project after these migrations are pushed

## 4. Boundaries (unchanged from Phase 1, repeated because they still apply)

1. Never bypass RLS; no service-role key outside a local dev script with a stated reason.
2. Never trust a client-passed `tenant_id` — resolve server-side, same pattern as Phase 1's helper functions.
3. Never log patient PII/PHI — this phase is where real patient names, phones, and clinical notes enter the system for the first time. `rules.md` §1.3 is no longer a hypothetical concern; it's live data now. Re-check every `console.log`/error message you write against this.
4. No new backend server, ORM, or hosting provider.
5. Every table ships with RLS from the migration that creates it.
6. Migrations are additive history — new migration to change something, never edit an applied one.
7. Do not touch `apps/web`. Flag anything you think needs to change there instead of touching it.
8. Don't build invite email delivery (§2.3). Don't build IPD, lab orders, or nurse task boards — that's Phase 3.
